title: Tarasius and the Synod receive and adore image-pictures in Christ’s and the saints’ names—‘so the whole holy Synod believes and teaches’
source_text: V. In eodem quoque Concilio, Actione secunda, perlecta Adriani Papae Epistola ad Tharasium, Rogantibus Papae Legatis num illi consentiret nec ne, inter alia respondet Tharasius, Concordamus & vim litterarum istarum confirmamus: & imaginum picturas, secundum priscam Patrum nostrorum traditionem, recipimus, & has desiderio nostro adoramus, ut in nomine Christi Dei nostri, & intemeratae Dominae nostrae Deiparae Virginis, sanctorumque Angelorum & omnium sanctorum factas. Quibus Tharasii verbis ipsa Synodus subjunxit, Universa sancta Synodus sic credit, & sic docet. Ejusdem Tomi pag. 313. litt. B.
pass_a_gloss: In the same Council also, in the second Action, when the Epistle of Pope Adrian to Tarasius had been read, the Pope’s Legates asking whether he agreed or not, Tarasius among other things answers, We agree and confirm the force of those letters: and we receive the pictures of images according to the ancient tradition of our Fathers, and we adore them with our desire, as made in the name of Christ our God, and of our undefiled Lady the Mother of God the Virgin, and of the holy Angels and of all the saints. To which words of Tarasius the Synod itself subjoined, The whole holy Synod thus believes, and thus teaches. Same Tom. p. 313, letter B.
pass_b_english: At Nicaea II Tarasius, with the Synod, receives image-pictures by ancient tradition and adores them in Christ’s and the saints’ names.
The whole Synod seals it: ‘thus we believe and teach.’

lemmas.gloss: we receive the pictures of images

choices.why: Corporate reception of image-adoration, not a private aside.
